runs.prompt:
Create one character design sheet for the original fictional character Mama.
Output: one opaque PNG, exactly 1536 × 1024 pixels, landscape 3:2.
Target asset: sheets/mama_sheet.png.

REFERENCE
Input image 1: the approved sheets/sasha_sheet.png.
Use it as the visual reference for paper material, texture scale, palette, rendering, compact sheet layout, and family resemblance in the nose and eyebrows. Do not depict Sasha or copy his age, hairstyle, clothing, or child proportions. The written Mama specification below governs her design.

COMPOSITION
Show exactly four depictions of the SAME woman on one unified cream sheet:
• Three intact full-body views, arranged left to right: front, left-facing profile, back.
• One smaller front-facing head-and-shoulders portrait to their right.

Center the full-body views approximately at x=400, x=620, and x=845. Use identical scale and aligned head and foot levels across these three views. Keep each complete silhouette within y=220..680, including hair, hands, and slippered feet. Use relaxed standing poses with arms resting naturally; keep hands readable and clear of the clothing silhouette.

Center the portrait approximately at x=1150, y=420. Include the complete hair silhouette, eyes, shoulders, and neckline. Keep the hair clip in its actual rear position; show only the portion naturally visible from the front. Do not move it to the forehead or temple for visibility.

Maintain clear gaps between all four depictions. Uniformly scale whole figures to fit; never crop, compress, or omit body parts. The portrait is a conventional connected bust, not an assembly of detached parts.

Keep ALL artwork and local shadows within x=96..1440 and y=200..700. Leave y=0..199 and y=701..1023 as uninterrupted cream paper background. These stricter bounds also satisfy the wider safe area of x=96..1440, y=128..752 and keep the entire bottom 30 percent empty. Never draw coordinate guides, borders, or labels.

CHARACTER — FIXED ACROSS ALL VIEWS
Mama is Sasha’s 38-year-old mother: an adult woman of medium build with mature adult proportions, a warm, slightly tired face, and a gentle expression. In the story she is clearly taller than a 12-year-old boy; the independent scale of this sheet does not establish her height relative to Sasha.

Skin: warm cream paper.
Face: large kind dark eyes, faint smile lines at the eye corners, a small straight nose, eyebrows sharing Sasha’s underlying structure, and a gentle small mouth.
Hair: shoulder-length dark chestnut hair, constructed from shaded brick-brown and warm-gray paper, pulled back and secured at the back with exactly one plain mustard hair clip.
Clothing: a soft faded olive-green housecoat with a small mustard flower pattern integrated into the paper material, a plain cream apron over it, and faded teal slippers.
No jewelry or glasses.

Preserve the same identity, apparent age, build, facial structure, hair length, clip placement, garment construction, and colors across all four depictions. Let visibility change naturally with the viewing angle.

PAPER MATERIAL AND LIGHT
Match the approved Sasha sheet’s handmade multilayer paper-collage rendering and warm, gently faded family-photo-album colors.

Build the character from overlapping pieces of matte colored paper with clearly visible natural fibers, slightly uneven cut or torn edges, and thin cream fiber rims. Use flat forms with restrained paper-tone variation. Create shallow depth through separate paper layers and soft, short contact shadows under upper-left illumination.

Construct faces with small cut-paper shapes and restrained dark ink-like details in shaded palette colors. Fibers must read as physical paper material, not an applied noise filter.

Use a plain cream #F1E6CF paper background with subtle inherent fibers and soft local shadows only. No room backdrop, floor line, or scenery.

PALETTE
Use only these six base colors with restrained light and shadow variations:
• Mustard yellow #D9A441
• Cream #F1E6CF
• Brick brown #8C4A32
• Olive green #7A7F3F
• Faded teal #5E8C8A
• Warm gray #A59B8C

Use cream for skin and pale fibers; shaded brick brown and warm gray for dark hair, eyes, eyebrows, and facial details. No pure-white or pure-black flat colors. No red #D92F2B anywhere; no magnet or other prop.

EXCLUSIONS
No additional people or character designs.
No panels, dividers, view labels, detached limbs, puppet rigs, or assembly diagrams.
No text, letters, numerals, pseudo-writing, logos, watermarks, signatures, captions, speech bubbles, arrows, annotation marks, motion lines, impact bursts, sparkles, or drawn effects.
No props, modern devices, brands, blood, wounds, or weapons.
No black outlines, photographic skin, smooth vector rendering, glossy plastic, or 3D rendering.
No film grain, noise overlays, vignette, blur, lens effects, or transitions; those are added later in code.

FINAL CHECK
The finished sheet contains three complete, equally scaled turnaround views and one smaller connected portrait of the same adult woman. Verify identity and clothing continuity, intact anatomy, visible slippered feet, rear clip placement, the six-color palette, and completely empty cream margins. Return only the finished image.

REFERENCE ATTACHMENTS CLARIFICATION:
Image 1 is the approved Sasha sheet: PRIMARY reference for the paper texture, compact layout, restrained family-album colors, rendering, and family resemblance ONLY. Design Mama according to the written specification. The three turnaround views and portrait all depict ONE SAME Mama. Match the compact horizontal arrangement of image 1, keeping generous empty top and bottom margins.
Image 2 is an approved scene used ONLY as a secondary reference for handmade paper fibers, layer edges and upper-left contact-shadow lighting. Do not copy its people, athletic anatomy, setting, composition or colors outside the six explicitly specified Mama colors. The written six-color Mama palette and image 1 take precedence. Tetsu absent: no red anywhere. This is a new character design, not the boy or the scene cast. Produce the new Mama sheet only, exactly 1536x1024 opaque PNG.
